summary: "Smart Recycling and the Sustainability" is an intelligent software solution designed to transform agricultural waste into valuable resources, thereby fostering sustainable agriculture. Utilizing climate data from NASA (NASA POWER), the system allows users to specify a country, region, city, and season, as well as the area of land under cultivation. It then analyzes climatic conditions—such as temperature, humidity, precipitation, solar radiation, and wind speed. Furthermore, by assessing the climatic requirements of various crops, the software identifies the most suitable crops for cultivation and estimates the volume of waste likely to be generated. A "Digital Twin" simulation module calculates the potential for converting waste into compost and energy, quantifies energy savings, evaluates sustainability indicators, estimates the reduction in CO₂ emissions, and determines the economic value of the resulting outputs. The significance of this project lies in its ability to bridge smart sustainable agricultural management, optimal crop selection, waste estimation, and the recycling of resources into renewable energy. Its ultimate goal is to minimize resource waste, mitigate environmental impacts, and support scientifically and economically sound decision-making within the framework of a circular economy. This software is scalable and can be deployed as a standalone platform.
details:
Smart Recycling and the Sustainability Cycle – From Geospatial Data to Intelligent Systems for Converting Waste into Resources and Energy

"Smart Recycling and the Sustainability Cycle" is an innovative software platform that integrates NASA’s Earth observation and climate data with artificial intelligence, agricultural feasibility analysis, and smart waste-to-resource technologies. Its primary objective is to translate environmental and climatic information into actionable decisions for sustainable agriculture, organic waste management, and the recovery of renewable resources.

1- What does this project do, and how does it work?

The platform enables users to select geographic locations and analyze environmental and seasonal conditions using climate data sourced from NASA. The current software demo—presented for the 2026 Hackathon—covers locations across three continents and four countries (Iran, Turkey, the United States, and Germany), allowing for the assessment of specific sites and their agricultural conditions.

The application combines climatic parameters, seasonal data, and crop requirements to evaluate agricultural feasibility. The system is designed to help users understand how environmental conditions influence agricultural production and the management of organic waste.

A key component involves linking satellite-derived environmental data with a patented, innovative reactor. This reactor is capable of drying waste, converting it into organic fertilizer, purifying the resulting biogas, and recovering energy. The technology is designed to process recyclable organic waste—from agricultural, municipal, and industrial sources—and transform it into valuable resources such as compost and energy.

2- What are the benefits and intended impact?

•           Supporting sustainable agriculture through feasibility analyses based on climate and regional conditions.

•           Improving organic waste management, reducing environmental pollution, and achieving zero waste.

•           Promoting renewable energy recovery and reducing reliance on fossil fuels.

•           Supporting circular economy principles by transforming waste into useful resources.

•           Assisting farmers and managers in making more informed decisions regarding the cultivation of suitable and compatible crops.

Our long-term vision is to integrate space-based environmental artificial intelligence with existing, practical technologies that address real-world challenges on Earth. This software is designed to be upgradeable via a Windows installer and incorporates real-world data and analyses covering all five continents.

3- What tools, programming languages, hardware, or software have been used?

This project utilizes a web-based software architecture developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Python.

Its development encompasses the following:

•           NASA Earth observation and climate data sources, specifically NASA POWER.

•           Geographic location selection and interactive mapping.

•           Analysis of climate and seasonal data.

•           Assessment of agricultural feasibility based on local environmental conditions and crop requirements.

•           Data visualization and analytical software components.

•           A "digital twin" conceptual framework that links environmental data with processes for converting waste into valuable resources.

The physical technology associated with this project is an innovative, multi-functional reactor designed for drying, composting, and treating exhaust gases. Developed by the technical team, a one-ton, semi-industrial prototype has been constructed and field-tested.

4. How is this project creative and innovative?

The creativity of the "Smart Recycling and Sustainability Cycle" lies in connecting two domains that are rarely integrated into a single operational platform: space-based environmental intelligence and technology for converting waste into valuable resources and energy.

Rather than using NASA data solely for observation, this project explores how satellite-derived climate information can support agricultural decision-making, as well as improve the planning of organic waste treatment and resource recovery. Integrating geographic analysis, seasonal assessment, agricultural feasibility, and an innovative waste-processing reactor creates a new approach to connecting space science with sustainable development.

5- What factors did the team take into consideration?

Our team—comprising Arman Naderi (PhD in Soil Science); Seyed Ali Hashemi (reactor inventor, software expert, and programmer); Siavash Hosseini Kamkar (IT and web development specialist); Seyed Hesam Hashemi (coder); and other team members—conducted a scientific and practical study of several key factors on a 40-hectare farm (previously used for tomato cultivation). These findings were then implemented within this platform, resulting in superior outcomes when cultivating potatoes.

The factors considered include: 1) climatic variations and seasonal changes; 2) agricultural requirements and the suitability of the local environment and climate; 3) geographical and climatic differences across various countries; 4) environmental protection and the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions; and 5) the accessibility, scalability, and practical execution of the project, as well as the necessity of transforming scientific data into understandable, actionable information.

Our ultimate goal is to demonstrate how NASA’s space-based data can facilitate the creation of smarter agricultural systems, more efficient waste management, and a sustainable circular economy—effectively turning environmental challenges into valuable resources
